verdict.rationale: Basecamp's own Client mode lets a project owner decide what clients should and shouldn't see, project by project. That is real, product-native view-access control, but the evidence covers only client visibility and says nothing about granular roles or edit permissions. missing for 10: documented role definitions (admin/owner/member etc.), edit-level permission controls, granular per-item or per-tool permissions, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a product manager, I can assign granular permissions and roles to control who can view or edit work

citations.quote: Basecamp’s Client mode lets you decide what they should — and shouldn’t — see, project by project.
